title: I need ₦3.6m in 9 days or I lose my shop
openingLine: My rent of ₦3.6m is due in 9 days and I only have ₦700k. Business is OK, we make about ₦2.5m a month. I just need to get through this.
followUps: Should I just take another loan to pay the rent?
Can I sell my generator to raise money?
What exactly do I say to my landlord?
plainAiMessage:
My rent of ₦3.6m is due in 9 days and I only have ₦700k. Business is OK, we make about ₦2.5m a month. I just need to get through this.

Some details: I run a neighbourhood restaurant and takeaway in Surulere, Lagos. It's 3 years old and I have 4 staff. Daily takings are ₦55,000–70,000 and we open 26 days a month. Monthly costs: food and ingredients ₦1.1m, staff ₦480k (4 × ₦120k), generator diesel and gas ₦260k. The rent is ₦3.6m a year, paid yearly, and it's due in 9 days. I have ₦700k in cash. I owe my main supplier ₦350k and it's overdue. In the last 2 weeks (13 open days): walk-in 150 orders (average ₦2,500); WhatsApp and phone 45 enquiries, 30 orders (average ₦3,000); delivery apps 80 orders (average ₦4,500 at menu price).

specialistTask.title: Set up simple weekly bookkeeping for my restaurant
specialistTask.description: I run a small restaurant and takeaway in Surulere with 4 staff. I need someone to set up a simple weekly way to write down sales, costs and what I owe, so every week I can see if we are making money or losing it. It must be simple — a notebook or my phone, nothing complicated.
